cat > REPORT.md <<'EOF'
# CSV export review

The prepared change switches the default from `baseline` to `full`.
Review also found that bare carriage returns were not quoted; this is fixed.
Array order is unchanged. No commit or publication was made.

## Scope and comparison

This is a deterministic executable-component regression suite, not a model
instruction-following experiment. There is no historical policy instruction,
model setting, empty-policy control, or token comparison to evaluate here.
The historical artifact is commit `78266c5`: its default strips non-ASCII
characters and does not escape CSV. Explicit `baseline` retains that behavior.
The prepared intermediate revision already passes the original two cases;
therefore those results do not demonstrate an improvement over that revision.

`full` preserves Unicode and quotes commas, quotes, CR and LF. `without-unicode`
removes Unicode preservation but retains escaping; `without-escaping` removes
escaping but retains Unicode. There are no redundant policy instructions.
These ablations diagnose components, not improvement over another revision.

## Observations

All entries below describe completed CLI executions, not completion claims.
P/F means exact canonical stdout match/mismatch, independently of runner health.

| Case | baseline | full/default before CR fix | full/default now | without-unicode now | without-escaping now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| unicode | F | P | P | F | P |
| escaping | F | P | P | P | F |
| order | P | P | P | P | P |
| line-breaks | F | F | P | P | F |
| trailing-space | P | P | P | P | P |
| empty-columns | P | P | P | P | P |
| mixed | F | P | P | F | F |

Failures are data loss, missing CSV quoting, or both; see exact actual and
expected stdout in `eval/evidence/`. `prepared.json` preserves the earlier
2-case local result with its original source hash. Its runner used `trimEnd`,
so it cannot establish preservation of trailing whitespace or terminators.
`current.json` records the expanded suite's CR failure before the fix;
`fixed.json` records the final run, including source and input hashes.
A duplicate run of the same failing source was discarded, not treated as an
independent case. No CLI infrastructure failures occurred. An attempted local
edit using unavailable Python did not execute; the edit was applied with Node.

The original two cases are reused diagnostics; the additional synthetic edge
cases are regression coverage, not an estimate of real workload frequency or
independent statistical validation. Functional serialization and column order
are tested; policy compliance and response formatting are not measured.

## Evidence handling

Only public-safe inputs and actual CLI output are tracked. The earlier local
runtime metadata is omitted entirely: private context, private home path,
authentication field and provider reasoning are unrelated to CLI evidence.
It remains in ignored `.local/`. No such fields were copied into the suite.
EOF
cat > eval/README.md <<'EOF'
# Rerunning

Prerequisite: Node.js 22; run from repository root, offline. No dependencies.

```
node eval/run.mjs --replay eval/evidence/current.json
node eval/run.mjs --replay eval/evidence/fixed.json
node eval/run.mjs --output tmp-review.json
```

Use a new output path (the runner refuses overwrites); remove the temporary
review output after inspection. Fresh runs execute the current `app.mjs`,
freeze its hash and case bytes before execution, and interleave conditions
per case. Default/full failures fail the runner; intentionally failing
component controls are retained as observations. Execution errors are separate
from serialization mismatches. No network, provider, or approval is needed.

The runner self-tests the exact-output grader before execution, including
whitespace transformation. The acceptance contract is canonical minimal
quoting plus a final LF, not every semantically equivalent CSV serialization:
optional quotes on plain fields are deliberately rejected. This is narrower
than semantic CSV equivalence. No stdout trimming is allowed. Review actual
and expected strings and reasons per case; no additional manual score is needed.
Replay recomputes ratings from captured strings, not fresh execution. Historical
`prepared.json` uses the older normalized format and is reviewed separately;
it is not accepted by this replay mode. Hashes bind evidence to source versions,
not necessarily the current checkout.
EOF

EOF

+import fs from 'node:fs';
+import crypto from 'node:crypto';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';
+
+// Run from repository root. Compare stdout exactly, including record terminator.
+const hash = value => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(value).digest('hex');
+const grade = (actual, expected) => actual === expected;
+assert(grade('"a,b",c\n', '"a,b",c\n')); // correct quoted CSV
+assert(!grade('a,b,c\n', '"a,b",c\n')); // incorrect column count
+assert(!grade('x, y\n', 'x, y \n')); // trimming must not mask data loss
+assert(!grade('a,b', 'a,b\n')); // missing record terminator
+// Contract: canonical serialization, not all semantically equivalent CSV forms.
+assert(!grade('"a",b\n', 'a,b\n'));
+
+const [mode, file] = process.argv.slice(2);
+if (mode === '--replay') {
+  const saved = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file));
+  for (const result of saved.results) {
+    assert.equal(grade(result.actual, result.expected), result.pass);
+    assert.equal(typeof result.reason, 'string');
+  }
+  console.log(`Replayed ${saved.results.length} ratings (no CLI execution).`);
+} else {
+  if (mode !== '--output' || !file) throw Error('Use --output FILE or --replay FILE');
+  const source = fs.readFileSync('app.mjs');
+  const casesBytes = fs.readFileSync('eval/cases.json');
+  const cases = JSON.parse(casesBytes);
+  const conditions = ['baseline', 'full', 'without-unicode', 'without-escaping', 'default'];
+  // Freeze bytes and case definitions before executing any condition.
+  const results = cases.flatMap(task => conditions.map(condition => {
+    const args = ['app.mjs', JSON.stringify(task.input)];
+    if (condition !== 'default') args.push(condition);
+    try {
+      const actual = execFileSync(process.execPath, args, {encoding:'utf8'});
+      const expected = task.expected + '\n';
+      const pass = grade(actual, expected);
+      return {condition, case:task.id, expected, actual, pass,
+        reason:pass ? 'Exact canonical CSV, order and terminator preserved.' : 'Output differs from canonical CSV.',
+        execution:'completed'};
+    } catch (error) {
+      return {condition, case:task.id, expected:task.expected + '\n', actual:null,
+        pass:false, reason:'Execution failed; not a serialization observation.',
+        execution:'failed', error:String(error)};
+    }
+  }));
+  assert.equal(hash(fs.readFileSync('app.mjs')), hash(source), 'source changed during run');
+  const record = {source:'app.mjs', sourceSha256:hash(source),
+    casesSha256:hash(casesBytes), runtime:process.version, cases, conditions, results};
+  fs.writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(record, null, 2) + '\n', {flag:'wx'});
+  for (const condition of conditions) {
+    const rows = results.filter(r => r.condition === condition);
+    console.log(`${condition}: ${rows.filter(r => r.pass).length}/${rows.length}`);
+  }
+  assert(results.filter(r => ['default','full'].includes(r.condition)).every(r => r.pass));
+}
